judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whereas clauses enumerate a long list of purposes (flood reduction, water supply, fisheries, hydroelectric power, pollution abatement) and then trail off into 'and for other purposes', leaving the reach of the recited purposes uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recitals of this kind were used in the fracking litigation to argue that the operative definition of 'project' in Section 1.2(g) and the review power in Section 3.8 reach only water-resource works; that is a classic recital-versus-operative-text tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure naming provision; the stray double period after 'Short title..' is a typographical slip that changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2(c) defining 'Compact' as Part I of the act; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The escape clause 'except as may be otherwise required by the context' makes every defined term contextually variable, which is itself an open-ended and contestable qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on whether 'project' in Section 3.8 must carry the Article 1.2(g) definition, which is exactly the fight the definitions section invites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Area of drainage into the Delaware River and its tributaries, including Delaware Bay' is a definite geographic test with only marginal edge cases.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.7's basin-limited jurisdiction and Section 1.2(e)'s 'within or without the basin' language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple naming definition with no evaluative or open-ended term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 2.1 creating the Commission; no inconsistency anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'Compact' as Part I of the act, a mechanical cross-reference with no vague term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument repeatedly slips between 'this act' and 'this compact' (e.g., Sections 1.1, 12.13, 14.21), a mild but real drafting inconsistency this definition must absorb.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net induced adverse effects, whether or not compensated for' is an economically loaded and boundary-less phrase within a cost definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Sections 11.4 and 12.2 on cost allocation, but nothing there contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Facility' piles a sweeping catch-all ('any and all things and appurtenances necessary, useful or convenient', 'or to facilitate any other uses of any of them') onto a list of specifics, squarely raising ejusdem generis/list-scope problems.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is incorporated into the 'project' definition in Section 1.2(g) and into Sections 3.6 and 3.8, so its breadth directly affects the reach of the Commission's review power that was actually litigated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any appropriate branch, department, bureau or division thereof, as the case may be' is loose but is unlikely to be outcome-determinative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits comfortably with Section 1.2(h) and the federal reservations in Section 15.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'project' is grammatically tangled ('any work, service or activity which is separately planned, financed, or identified by the commission, or any separate facility undertaken ... for the conservation, utilization, control, development or management of water resources'), and whether the qualifying purpose phrase modifies both branches is genuinely contestable; this is the ambiguity litigated over natural gas well pads.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its meaning must be squared with Section 3.8's 'no project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin', with the preamble's water-focused purposes, and with Sections 3.6(b) and 13.1, which pull in different directions on breadth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite membership definition with no evaluative language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Preamble's list of parties and Section 14.22.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Water and related natural resources in, on, under, or above the ground, including related uses of land, which are subject to beneficial use' is extremely broad and its outer boundary (does it capture subsurface gas, land use generally?) is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the operative limit in Sections 3.8, 3.6(b) and 13.1, so how far it reaches determines the Commission's jurisdiction over activities the preamble never mentions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory phrase carrying no substantive term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It frames findings that are echoed in the preamble; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A declaratory finding of public purpose with no operative test to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.3(b) and 14.3; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statement of sovereign right and joint exercise; declaratory rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside Sections 5.5 and 11.3 reserving state authority, which it broadly matches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A single administrative agency is therefore essential' is a finding, not a rule, and offers little to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably cuts against Section 1.5's directive to preserve existing agencies and Sections 11.1(c)/11.2(c) preserving other agencies' authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A forecast-style finding ('ample to meet all presently projected demands') that states no obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its optimism about supply sits oddly with Article 10's protected-area and emergency shortage machinery, though as a finding it does not truly conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To make secure and protect present developments within the states' and 'equal and uniform treatment to all water users who are similarly situated' are open-textured purpose language used to argue about the Commission's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A purposes clause of this kind pulls against the broad regulatory grants in Sections 3.8 and 10.1, and courts routinely invoke it against expansive readings of those sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard non-derogation clause preserving congressional powers, definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(t) makes the whole federal participation contingent on this section's constitutionality and 15.1(b) is expressly subordinated to it, so its scope has cross-instrument bite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent not inconsistent with the compact' and 'to the fullest extent it finds feasible and advantageous' are elastic standards resting on the Commission's own judgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 7.4(b) and 8.2(b) expressly invoke this section as a constraint on Commission operation, while Section 1.3(c) declares a single agency essential — a real pull in two directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal notice window — 'not later than 20 years nor sooner than 25 years prior to the termination' — is awkwardly inverted phrasing that a reader can easily take as an impossible window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the compact sets a termination mechanic, though Section 1.6(b) assumes termination 'by operation of paragraph (a)' which speaks only of notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terminated by operation of paragraph (a)' is a compressed cross-reference, since (a) speaks of notice rather than operation, but the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves wind-up 'in such manner as may be provided by act of the Congress' even though the states are equal signatories, a mild asymmetry against Sections 1.3(b) and 14.20.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A creation clause with settled corporate-law terms and no evaluative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.1's corporate powers and Section 15.1(m) providing the Commission is not a federal agency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To serve during the term of office of the President' is a definite tenure formula; no ambiguity on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument's own endnote records that this section and Section 15.1(d) ('shall serve at the pleasure of the President') were inconsistent as to the federal member's term until 1997 — an acknowledged internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite appointment and removal mechanics, with the only softness being 'unless otherwise provided by law of the signatory party'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(d) overrides the tenure rule for the federal alternate, and the endnote/WRDA material adds a further designation regime, so the section does not stand alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for necessary expenses' is clear, with 'necessary' the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) expressly permits the federal member and advisor to be paid 'the provisions of Sections 2.4 and 2.6 notwithstanding', a direct carve-out from this rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A majority of the membership' can be read as a majority of all seats or of those present, a small but real lexical ambiguity in a voting rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Other provisions require unanimity (Sections 3.3(a), 13.3(b)(2)) or 'a majority of the full membership' (Section 14.5(a)), and the differing formulations invite argument about what this baseline means.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Organizational housekeeping with definite duties; nothing vague enough to litigate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) carves the advisor out of the no-compensation regime and New York's Section 632 elaborates the advisor role, but neither contradicts this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary or convenient to effectuate its powers or duties within the basin' is an elastic extraterritorial trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the 'within or without the basin' language in Section 1.2(e) and the sale powers in Article 9; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad statement of mission using 'shall develop and effectuate plans, policies and projects', mandatory in form but with no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'projects' in an apparently looser sense than the Section 1.2(g) definition, a small strain against the definitions article.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory cross-reference to Article 13.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 13 (Sections 13.1–13.3) tracks the same three instruments, so the cross-reference holds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, definite duty to adopt a comprehensive plan after consultation; 'interested public bodies' is only mildly soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 states the same duty in fuller terms, and the two are consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All public and private projects affecting the basin' and 'such reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine' are broad and self-defined boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.2 restates the program requirement with a six-year default period, so the two overlap without squarely conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite budgeting duty with no evaluative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.3 elaborates the same budgets consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Invokes 'the doctrine of equitable apportionment', an external legal standard whose content is contested but which is at least a recognised term of art.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(b) then says no allocation 'shall be deemed to constitute an apportionment of the waters of the basin among the parties', which sits uneasily with an allocation power exercised under the apportionment doctrine.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A state of emergency resulting from a drought or catastrophe' is somewhat open, but the unanimous-consent mechanics are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 3.4, 3.5 and 10.4, and the interlocking decree carve-outs are drafted to be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso preserving covenants 'with a duration not exceeding the life of this compact' is clear, but the disclaimer that no allocation constitutes an apportionment is conceptually strained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably contradicts the opening of Section 3.3, which grants allocation power 'in accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any proper party deeming itself aggrieved' leaves 'proper party' undefined anywhere in the compact, and 'out-of-basin diversion' is not defined either.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Proper party' recurs in Section 3.4 without definition and the review route here (Supreme Court original jurisdiction) sits beside the general 'court of competent jurisdiction' route used in Sections 3.8, 10.6 and 15.1(p).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense waiver with nested exceptions and an undefined 'proper party'; the double exception clause is hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with Sections 3.3(a), 3.3(c) and 3.5, and New York's Section 633 adds a further state consent condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To this end, and without limitation thereto' introduces a non-exhaustive list of prohibitions, leaving the reach of the general prohibition uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly subordinates itself to Sections 3.3 and 3.4, and Section 3.8 is in turn made subject to it, so the pieces are designed to interlock.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Impede or interfere with' rights under the decree is a broad but familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the introductory sentence of Section 3.5 and with Section 3.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on fees for decree-permitted diversions; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.7 grants a general rate power and Section 15.1(b) adds a further federal restriction, but both are drafted as compatible carve-outs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but definite jurisdictional carve-out tied to the decree; 'used in connection with' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 3.8's approval power expressly, so the relationship is stated rather than left implicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence with an explicit consent exception; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the river master consultation contemplated by Section 3.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare permissive introduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere contradicts the framing of Section 3.6 as an enabling list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Necessary, convenient or useful for the purposes of this compact' is an open-ended self-judged standard attached to a long verb string.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth must be reconciled with the limits in Sections 4.5, 9.3 and 3.5 that forbid particular activities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All projects and facilities in the basin which affect its water resources, including without limitation thereto' followed by enumerated examples is a textbook general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'affect its water resources' trigger is broader than Section 3.8's 'substantial effect' test, and the two standards do not sit easily together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Another 'including without limitation thereto' list, but the power is only to research and report, so the catch-all carries little consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(e), 6.4 and 14.12 on data and reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or other purposes' is an untethered catch-all at the end of an enumerated list of uses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Section 6.4's warning and posting power; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow investigative power tied to administering the comprehensive plan; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 3.6(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An information and reporting power with no operative test to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps harmlessly with Section 14.12's reporting duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As the commission may deem necessary or desirable' is discretionary but the power to negotiate for aid is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.20(c) and 14.1(a)(2) on receiving grants and loans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such other and different powers' plus 'all powers necessary or convenient ... or which may be reasonably implied' is a sweeping catch-all sitting at the end of enumerated specifics, inviting ejusdem generis and expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read broadly it could swallow the express limits in Sections 4.5, 9.3 and 3.5, which is precisely the whole-instrument tension a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party' is emphatic and clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(b) expressly cuts down Section 3.7 for pre-existing free withdrawals and navigation charges, and Section 11.3 reserves state taxing powers, so the section cannot be read alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin' turns on two undefined evaluative terms — the scope of 'project' and what counts as a 'substantial effect' — and this is the sentence litigated over natural gas development.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on the Section 1.2(g) definition of 'project' and Section 1.2(i) 'water resources', and it must be squared with the preamble's water-focused purposes and with Sections 3.6(b), 11.1 and 11.2, which use different effect thresholds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'To this end, but with limitation thereto, the commission may' — an evident dropped 'out' that reverses the meaning of the limiting phrase, a mechanical error changing what the provision says.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel provisions (Sections 3.5, 4.1, 3.6(b)) all use 'without limitation thereto', confirming the error and creating an inconsistency across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short list of cooperative verbs with no evaluative test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 11.5 and 14.1(a)(1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or for any other purpose' is an unbounded catch-all following an enumerated list of engineering functions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.5's direction to employ existing agencies; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So far as consistent with the comprehensive plan' is a soft qualifier but the power itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Sections 13.1 and 3.8, both of which use the comprehensive plan as the touchstone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow enabling power to qualify as a sponsoring agency; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.6(g) and Section 15.1(o) limiting other federal agencies' participation.
